chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Isma'il ibn Marar, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'May I be your ransom, how is it that when a man dies and his children from the kinship are equal, the women inherit half of what the men inherit, while they are weaker than the men and less resourceful?' He said, 'Because Allah, the Exalted, has favored the men over the women by a degree, and because the women return as dependents upon the men.'
ai.seo_question: Why do women inherit half of what men inherit in Islam according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) elucidates the wisdom behind the female inheriting half the share of the male by linking it to the principle of *fadl* (divine preference) and the economic reality of *‘awla* (financial maintenance). This narration highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that inheritance shares are not merely about equality but are calibrated to the respective financial responsibilities, where men bear the burden of providing for their dependents.
